title: HEALTHY HABITS
goal: Students can talk about daily health habits, ask and give advice using should/shouldn't, and compare healthy choices.
goal_vi: Học sinh có thể nói về các thói quen sức khỏe hàng ngày, đưa ra lời khuyên với should/shouldn't và so sánh các lựa chọn lành mạnh.

grammar.title: Modal Verbs: Should / Shouldn't
grammar.explain_en: We use 'should' to give good advice and 'shouldn't' to warn against bad choices.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta dùng 'should' để đưa ra lời khuyên tốt và 'shouldn't' để khuyên không nên làm điều có hại.
examples: You should wash your hands before eating.
You should eat fresh fruit.
You shouldn't eat junk food before bed.

grammar.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous
grammar.explain_en: Use Present Simple for daily habits and Present Continuous for actions happening right now.
grammar.explain_vi: Thì Hiện tại đơn dùng cho thói quen hàng ngày, Hiện tại tiếp diễn dùng cho hành động đang diễn ra.
examples: I brush my teeth every morning.
Look! Mai is drinking water now.
We play sports every afternoon.
grammar.wrong: ❌ I am drink water every day.

grammar.title: Simple Comparatives (-er / more...)
grammar.explain_en: Add '-er' to short adjectives or use 'more' before long words to compare two habits.
grammar.explain_vi: Thêm '-er' vào tính từ ngắn hoặc dùng 'more' trước tính từ dài để so sánh hai thói quen.
examples: Running is faster than walking.
Apples are healthier than chips.
Exercising is more useful than watching TV.
grammar.wrong: ❌ Fruit is more healthy than soda.

grammar.title: Past Simple of Common Verbs
grammar.explain_en: Use past verbs like was, were, ate, drank, played to talk about what you did yesterday.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng quá khứ của động từ (was, were, ate, drank, played) để kể về hoạt động ngày hôm qua.
examples: Yesterday I was active at the park.
I ate vegetables for dinner last night.
Minh drank warm milk before sleep.

readings.title: MAI'S HEALTHY DAY
readings.text: Mai is nine years old. She lives in Hanoi with her family. Mai has many healthy habits. Every morning, she wakes up early at six o'clock. She brushes her teeth and washes her hands with soap. Then she drinks a warm glass of water. For breakfast, Mai eats eggs and fresh fruit. She walks to school with her friend Lan. At school, she plays jump rope during break time. In the evening, she eats green vegetables for dinner. Mai never goes to bed late. She sleeps at nine o'clock every night. Mai feels strong, happy, and ready for school.

readings.title: NAM'S HEALTHY CHANGE
readings.text: Last year, Nam was not very healthy. He liked playing video games for hours and went to sleep late at night. He ate a lot of junk food like chips and drinking sweet soda. He was often tired at school and sometimes got sick. Two months ago, his doctor told him to change his daily habits. Now, Nam works hard to build good habits! He drinks three bottles of water every day. He eats red apples and fresh carrots for snack. After school, he plays football with Minh and Ben in the school yard. He also stops playing video games at eight in the evening. Yesterday, Nam went to bed at nine o'clock and slept very well. Today, he feels happier, stronger, and more active than last year.

readings.title: THE SCHOOL HEALTH CLUB
readings.text: Welcome to the Grade 4 Health Club presentation! Today, Linh and Tom are sharing three simple rules for a healthy life. First, choose good fuel for your body. Your body is like a super car; it needs clean fuel to run fast. Eating vegetables, fruits, fish, and drinking plenty of pure water gives you maximum power. Junk food with too much sugar will slow you down. Second, keep your body active every day. You should exercise for at least thirty minutes daily. You can run, swim, ride a bike, or dance to active music. Exercising makes your heart strong and your brain sharp. Third, give your body enough rest. Sleep is the best medicine for a tired body. Children aged nine should sleep nine to ten hours every night. When you sleep, your body grows and repairs itself. Yesterday, our club surveyed fifty students in our school. We found that students who sleep early and eat fruits every day get higher marks in class! Let us build healthy habits together starting from today!

listening.script: Hello Grade 4 students! I am Doctor Ha from the city hospital. Today, I want to share important healthy habits with you. To stay healthy, you should eat good food every day. Vegetables like carrots and spinach are full of vitamins. You should also eat fresh fruits like oranges and apples. Drinking pure water is much healthier than drinking sweet soda. You need at least six glasses of water daily. Next, do not forget to keep your body moving! You can run, dance, or play sports with friends. Finally, go to bed early! Children should sleep nine hours every night to help their brains grow. Remember: good habits today mean a happy life tomorrow!

classroom_game.name: Healthy Choice Relay
steps_en: Place flashcards of foods and activities (fruit, soda, exercise, sleeping late) on a table across the room.
Divide the class into two teams standing in line.
Teacher shouts a category: 'Healthy Choice!' or 'Unhealthy Choice!'.
The first student from each team runs to the table, picks a matching card, and says a sentence: 'You should eat apples!' or 'You shouldn't drink soda!'.
The team with the most correct cards and clear sentences wins the game.
steps_vi: Đặt thẻ hình về đồ ăn và hoạt động (trái cây, nước ngọt, tập thể dục, thức khuya) ở bàn phía trên lớp.
Chia lớp thành hai đội xếp thành hàng dọc.
Giáo viên hô to nhóm: 'Lựa chọn lành mạnh!' hoặc 'Lựa chọn không lành mạnh!'.
Học sinh đầu tiên của mỗi đội chạy lên, chọn đúng thẻ và nói câu: 'You should eat apples!' hoặc 'You shouldn't drink soda!'.
Đội nào chọn đúng nhiều thẻ và nói câu chính xác nhất sẽ chiến thắng.
